subject: math-ai-sl
title: Fitting a crop model
stem:
A quadratic model $y=ax^2+bx+c$ is to pass exactly through the three observations.

| x | y |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | 10 |
| 1 | 17 |
| 3 | 25 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write three equations for the parameters.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use technology to find $a,b,c$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Predict $y$ at $x=4$.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain why this prediction is less secure than one for $x=2$.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: An independent observation at x=4 is 28. Find the residual (observed minus predicted) and explain its sign.

steps.text: Solve the simultaneous linear equations for the three coefficients.
Four lies outside the observed interval [0,3], so it is extrapolation; two is interpolation.
The positive residual means the model underestimates the observation by 2 units.

verification.method: Independent standard-library numerical and mathematical checks
verification.notes: All data points substituted into the fitted polynomial; coefficient system nonsingular. Rounding is to three significant figures unless otherwise specified.

subject: math-ai-sl
title: Market stall profit
stem: The daily profit, in USD, for selling $x$ batches is $P(x)=-2(x-2)(x-20)$, with $0\leq x\leq23$. Treat $x$ as continuous for modelling.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the break-even sales levels.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the maximum modelled profit and its sales level.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the interval for which the business makes a profit.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Give one limitation of treating $x$ as continuous.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Find a whole-number sales level giving the greatest profit, with supporting comparisons.

steps.text: The business can sell only a whole number of batches, so a fractional optimum may need comparison with adjacent integers.
Compare the adjacent integers around the continuous vertex; when the vertex itself is an integer, include it and its two neighbours.
$P(10)=160$, $P(11)=162$, $P(12)=160$ USD; choose 11 batches. Accept 11 if the maximum values tie.

verification.method: Independent standard-library numerical and mathematical checks
verification.notes: Quadratic roots, sign between roots and vertex checked numerically. Rounding is to three significant figures unless otherwise specified.
